title: Ep 002 – Carson Teagarden
guest_bio: Calisthenics athlete and online fitness coach (Home Shred). Built a coaching business and social following teaching bodyweight training, nutrition, and sustainable habits — and coached Dennis Yu through a 70-lb transformation.
summary: Calisthenics coach Carson Teagarden on fitness that lasts: consistency over intensity, two or three goals not fifty, why it's growth not pain, and accountability as the real difference-maker.
note: Chapter/quote timestamps are approximate — offset from the combined multi-episode Descript export. Re-export this episode individually for exact times.

chapters.title: Meet Carson: skinny kid to calisthenics coach
Diets are BS — fitness as a lifestyle built on consistency
Two or three goals, not fifty — the Apple-rings principle
What you say no to; George's 400-lb start & the book 'Evolved'
It's not pain, it's growth — the right expectation
Success isn't a straight line — plateaus & getting back on
Staying on the journey: training for longevity
No-excuses training: your living room is a gym
Holding Dennis accountable — 'is the cookie worth it?'
Share the journey publicly — that's the accountability
Dennis's 70-lb transformation & where to find Carson

pull_quotes.speaker: George Leith
pull_quotes.text: Diets are bullshit. Fitness isn't something that you try — it becomes a lifestyle.

pull_quotes.speaker: Carson Teagarden
pull_quotes.text: You don't get a six-pack the first day of training. It's that consistency.

pull_quotes.speaker: Carson Teagarden
pull_quotes.text: If you have too many goals, there's too much going on, and you can't do anything.

pull_quotes.speaker: George Leith
pull_quotes.text: As much as it's what you're doing, it's what you're not doing that leads to success.

pull_quotes.speaker: Carson Teagarden
pull_quotes.text: The day you miss because you're a little tired — those days add up.

pull_quotes.speaker: George Leith
pull_quotes.text: Your knees are gonna be sore. Put some ice on it, and get back out there tomorrow.

pull_quotes.speaker: Carson Teagarden
pull_quotes.text: Once they hit three, six months, they've got the momentum — and they love the process.

pull_quotes.speaker: Carson Teagarden
pull_quotes.text: I don't want to be 40 with all this pain. I think longevity — at 80 I want to be able to run.

pull_quotes.speaker: Carson Teagarden
pull_quotes.text: Is that cookie even worth it? To burn it takes me two, three miles of running.

pull_quotes.speaker: George Leith
pull_quotes.text: If you're not prepared to share that you're on a journey, I don't know how serious you are about it.

pull_quotes.speaker: George Leith
pull_quotes.text: In 2026, you're not getting anybody to buy in unless they believe you've been a part of that journey.
